summary: Three independent backend/frontend runs completed successfully. Core candidate registration, duplicate protection, email/phone login, auth/me, draft autosave, payment gating and verification, post-payment document upload, submission prerequisites/success, admin authorization and admin workflows, all requested public routes, navigation/footer, FAQ/countdown/tables, candidate dashboard, full apply flow, and admin UI were checked and working. The merged defects are: malformed admin application IDs return 500, MongoDB identifiers are exposed in API responses, credentialed CORS reflects arbitrary origins, and authentication has no HttpOnly cookie or brute-force lockout. One referenced auth playbook file was absent from the workspace.

critical.title: Malformed admin application ID returns HTTP 500
critical.steps_to_reproduce: Authenticate as the documented admin, then GET /api/admin/applications/not-a-valid-object-id and PATCH the same path/status with {"status":"submitted"}.
critical.expected: A malformed identifier should return a safe, consistent client error (400 or 404) rather than an internal server error.
critical.actual: GET returned HTTP 500 with a Mongoose CastError; the PATCH path uses the same unhandled ObjectId cast path and should be verified after the fix.
critical.impact: Normal invalid client input is treated as a server failure and leaks Mongoose/model details, polluting monitoring and weakening the API contract.

critical.title: CORS reflects arbitrary origins while credentials are enabled
critical.location: backend/src/app.js CORS middleware and backend/.env CORS_ORIGINS="*"
critical.steps_to_reproduce: Send an API request with an arbitrary Origin header to the external API and inspect the response headers/configuration. The deployed configuration maps CORS_ORIGINS="*" to cors({origin:true, credentials:true}).
critical.expected: Credentialed CORS should allow only explicit trusted frontend origin(s).
critical.actual: The wildcard configuration reflects the request origin and enables credentials for arbitrary origins.
critical.impact: Broadens cross-origin access and creates a security regression risk for authenticated APIs, especially if cookie authentication is introduced.

critical.title: Authentication lacks HttpOnly cookie and brute-force lockout
critical.steps_to_reproduce: Inspect a successful login response, then submit five consecutive wrong candidate-password attempts followed by the correct password.
critical.expected: Authentication should set a secure HttpOnly cookie and throttle or lock the account after repeated failures, as required by the auth security checks.
critical.actual: The app returns JWTs in JSON for localStorage use, sets no application HttpOnly auth cookie, and accepts the correct login immediately after five consecutive 401 responses without a 429/lockout.
critical.impact: A localStorage token is exposed to XSS and unlimited credential guessing remains possible absent another perimeter control.

minor.title: MongoDB internal _id fields are exposed in application, admin, and payment responses
minor.location: GET/PATCH /api/applications/me, POST /api/applications/me/documents, POST /api/applications/me/submit, POST /api/payments/verify, GET/PATCH /api/admin/applications* and GET /api/admin/payments
minor.steps_to_reproduce: Register/authenticate a candidate and inspect application/payment JSON responses; authenticate as admin and inspect application list/detail/status and payments responses. Admin UI/API consumers must use row['_id'] for detail/status calls.
minor.expected: Responses should use explicit safe DTOs/projections, exposing only an intentional public id/applicationNumber and omitting raw persistence fields such as _id and __v.
minor.actual: Controllers return Mongoose application/payment documents directly, including raw Mongo/Mongoose identifiers and persistence shape.
minor.impact: Internal database identifiers are unnecessarily exposed and the frontend/API contract is coupled to Mongo/Mongoose document representation.
